nrIncident.summary: Lines reopened: disruption between Brighton / Lewes and Gatwick Airport expected until the end of the day
nrIncident.routes:
Gatwick Express between Brighton and London Victoria
Southern between Ore / Eastbourne / Littlehampton / Brighton and London Victoria, and also between Eastbourne and Haywards Heath / London Bridge
Thameslink between Brighton and Gatwick Airport / Bedford / Cambridge, and also between Haywards Heath and Bedford
nrIncident.message:
The emergency services have completed their work following an earlier incident where a person was hit by a train. This has allowed all lines between Brighton and Haywards Heath to reopen. Whilst service recovers, trains may still be delayed by up to 45 minutes, revised or cancelled.
Disruption is expected until the end of the day.
If you've been affected by what happened on the network today, there is always someone to talk to. You can contact the Samaritans on 116 123 from any phone for a confidential chat.
Customer advice:
Southern and Thameslink services have now resumed running on most routes; however, some routes remain subject to delays and short-notice cancellations.
You can now use your normal route, though please check live departure boards before setting off an allow at least 20 minutes extra time to complete your journey.
Changes to services:
The following routes may still be impacted and subject to some delays and cancellations:
• Brighton and Bedford: Thameslink services are now running, though they may be subject to delays and short-notice cancellations
• Cambridge and Brighton: Thameslink services will remain subject to delays and cancellations for the remainder of the day
• Cambridge and London Kings Cross: Great Northern services will call additionally at Ashwell & Morden
If you are travelling to Gatwick Airport for a flight:
Services to Gatwick Airport have been disrupted and it will take at least 30 minutes longer than usual to travel to the airport. Please make sure to check your journey ahead of time as you may need to use an alternative route, and consider starting your journey earlier where possible.
If you are travelling between Brighton, London and Cambridge:
A reduced service is running on this route, and you may need to change between London St Pancras International and London Kings Cross for Great Northern services. If you are planning to travel, please allow at least 40 minutes more time to complete your journey.
Ticket acceptance on alternative routes:
You can use your ticket at no extra cost on:
• Southeastern services between Ashford International, Hastings, Tunbridge Wells and London
• Alternative Southern services between Brighton and London Victoria via Barnham
• Alternative Thameslink services between East Grinstead and London
• London Underground services between London terminals
Rail replacement buses are running a shuttle service for all stations between Haywards Heath and Brighton. Please check journey planner for the latest departure times.
Parking at alternative stations:
To help with your journey, season ticket holders between Brighton / Haywards Heath / Three Bridges / Uckfield / Lewes are allowed to park at any reasonable station between these points at no additional cost.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.
Stay up to date on the move with Southern’s WhatsApp channel. Live updates are available Monday to Friday, 07:00–21:00.
Can you tell me more about the incident?
A person has been hit by a train on this part of the network. Network Rail and the emergency services are responding to the incident and working to manage the situation as sensitively, quickly and safely as possible.
If you or someone close to you has been affected by this incident, support is available from the Samaritans. You can speak to someone at any time by calling 116 123, free of charge and from any phone. You don't have to face a difficult time alone.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.routes: Between London Charing Cross and Hayes (Kent) / Sevenoaks / Tunbridge Wells / Dartford / Maidstone East / Gravesend / Ramsgate
nrIncident.message:
A trespass incident was reported earlier this evening between Waterloo East and London Bridge, but all lines have now reopened.
Trains running to / from London Charing Cross may continue to be cancelled, delayed or revised to run to different stations to normal whilst service recovers.
Disruption is expected until 02:30.
What should I do?
You can use your ticket at no extra cost on the London Underground between London Terminals and on highspeed services between Dover Priory and London St Pancras International.
How can I stay up to date?
You can follow Southeastern on Twitter (X) @SE_Railway or follow the Southeastern WhatsApp channel.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
